title: Balanced sections of scalar-extended constant tensor coefficients
statement: Let k be a field, Y a scheme, g:Y → Spec(k), M a k-module, and G a Y-module. Using the constant scalar-extension tensor presheaf and scalar restriction of sections [lem-sc-picard-constant-sections-tensor-basis], there exist additive equivalences e_V: (picardConstantSectionsTensor k Y g M G)(V) ≃ M tensor_k G(V) for every open V. For every a in O_Y(V), s in M, and t in G(V), e_V(a • e_V⁻¹(s tensor t)) = s tensor (a • t). For every restriction V ⊆ U and section x over U, e_V(res(x)) = (id_M tensor res)(e_U(x)).

proof.text: Use the adopted-source construction picardConstantScalarExtensionSections for the linear equivalences q_V from O_Y(V) tensor_k M to the chosen pullback sections. Its theorem picardConstantScalarExtensionSections_map gives the pure-tensor restriction formula. This realizes the same scalar-extension comparison node directly, without the retired Sheaf existential wrapper.

Tensor q_V inverse with the identity on G(V), commute the factors, apply Mathlib TensorProduct.AlgebraTensorModule.cancelBaseChange, then commute the factors back. This gives the additive equivalence e_V with e_V(q_V(a tensor s) tensor t)=s tensor (a • t). Its inverse on s tensor t is q_V(1 tensor s) tensor t by injectivity and the forward formula. TensorProduct.tmul_smul proves the scalar-action identity. For restriction compatibility use tensor induction, surjectivity of q_U, and a second tensor induction. The pure-tensor case follows from the restriction formula for q, the forward formula, and G.val.map_smul. Zero and addition cases use the additive-map laws. No theorem with sorry is used.
